about: Tandem protocol v1 conformance cases (spec/protocol.md is the source of truth). probe: the app every host builds for this suite. root -> child (a stack) -> screens (bottom to top; the last is focused). Each action names a fixed behavior described in probe.behaviors; input is the action's schema or null. Lent actions come from the stack, then the root. cases: each case runs in a fresh host session (fresh app). Input bytes = each 'send' string UTF-8 encoded followed by one LF, then the raw bytes of 'sendHex' (hex digits, optional) appended as-is. padLine {index, bytes}: before sending, append ASCII spaces (0x20) to send[index] until its UTF-8 length is exactly 'bytes' (LF not counted). Close the input after sending. The host's whole stdout must equal each 'expect' string UTF-8 encoded followed by one LF, nothing else. Before comparing: replace {{platform}} in expected lines with the host's platform (swift or kotlin), and in every actual line apply the regex ^\{"error":\{"code":"([a-z]+)","message":"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*" -> {"error":{"code":"$1","message":"". Expected error lines carry "message":"", so only error.message is ignored; it must still be present and a string. rule: the spec rule the case checks (for humans).

behaviors.configure: state.meta = {tag: input.meta.tag, level: input.meta.level or 0, pinned: input.meta.pinned or false}
behaviors.pop: pop the stack's top screen; with one screen left, do nothing (ok:true, unchanged)
behaviors.reset: rebuild the whole app in its initial state (stack = [Home, Probe] with initial states)

cases.rule: No bytes, no lines, no responses.
A CR before the LF is ignored.
CR+LF alone is an empty line: json error.
An empty line is a json error; the session continues.
A blank (whitespace-only) line is a json error.
A line starting with a byte order mark is a json error.
json is checked before handshake; a failed line does not count as hello.
A line with invalid UTF-8 (0xFF) is a json error.
Overlong (C0 AF), encoded surrogate (ED A0 80) and truncated (E2 82) UTF-8 are json errors.
Bytes after the last LF count as one more line.
A trailing partial line without LF is still answered.
One response per line, in order; input ending in LF has no extra empty line after it.
After an error the session continues with the next line.
A line of exactly 1 MiB (1048576 bytes, LF excluded) is accepted; trailing JSON whitespace is padding.
A line longer than 1 MiB is a json error.
Nesting of exactly 64 levels is allowed (then the non-object is a request error).
Nesting deeper than 64 levels is a json error.
Depth counts the outer object: object + 64 arrays = 65 levels, json error.
Object + 63 arrays = 64 levels: parsed, then rejected as an unknown field.
A duplicate key is a json error.
A duplicate key at any level is a json error, before any input check.
Duplicate keys inside an object inside an array are a json error.
Keys are compared after unescaping: "o\u0070" duplicates "op".
Malformed JSON is a json error.
A raw control character inside a JSON string is invalid JSON.
JSON whitespace between tokens is allowed.
Anything other than hello before a successful hello is a handshake error (no path).
do before hello is a handshake error and changes nothing.
hello with an unsupported version is a version error with supported:[1]; it may be retried.
Versions 0 and -1 are version errors.
hello.version must be an integer: "1", 1.0, 1e0, null and a missing version are request errors.
Unknown fields are rejected on hello; the failed hello does not complete the handshake.
A request that is not an object is a request error without path.
A missing op is a request error at $.op.
A non-string op is a request error at $.op.
An unknown op is a request error at $.op; op is case-sensitive.
ls takes no fields.
do rejects unknown fields and changes nothing.
do without action is a request error at $.action.
do.action must be a string.
do.input must be an object when present; null, arrays and strings are request errors.
json beats request.
request beats handshake.
handshake beats action and input.
request beats version.
A mistyped input field is a request error even when the action is unknown.
action beats input.
do with an action the focused screen does not offer is an action error at $.action.
Action names are exact.
After Back, the previous screen's actions are gone.
Own actions first, then lent ones nearest container first; the shadowed App.Reset is not listed.
Back (lent by Stack) pops to Home: name, path and from change; App lends Reset after Stack's Back.
Back with one screen left is an app rule, not an error: ok and unchanged.
Probe and App both offer Reset; Probe's (nearest) wins and only zeroes count.
On Home, App's Reset is reachable and rebuilds the app.
An action without schema takes no input.
input given to an action without schema is an input error at $.input, even {}.
A required integer.
A missing required field is an input error at its path; omitted input counts as {}.
9007199254740991 is a valid integer.
9007199254740992 is out of range.
-9007199254740991 is a valid integer.
-9007199254740992 is out of range.
1.0, 1e2, 1E2, 0.5 and "1" are not integers.
true, [1] and {} are not integers.
Integers are written in plain decimal.
null is never valid, even for an optional field.
Object schemas are closed.
Keys compare by exact code units; escapes decode first.
An optional field may be left out; input itself may be omitted.
A string field rejects other types.
enum allows only the listed strings.
Strings compare by exact code units: decomposed "cafe\u0301" is not "caf\u00e9".
An array of strings, including empty.
A wrong element is reported at its index.
A non-array is rejected at the array's path.
A nested closed object; optional nested fields may be left out. Nested keys are sorted on output.
Nested errors carry nested paths.
A failed request changes nothing.
Keys sort by UTF-16 code units: U+1F600 (D83D DE00) sorts before U+FF61; uppercase before lowercase.
Only ", \ and controls are escaped; \b \f \n \r \t, else lowercase \u00XX; / and DEL are raw.
Non-ASCII is written as raw UTF-8, whether it arrived raw or escaped.
